Plot predictions

Source: R/predict.R
plot.stareal_pred.Rd

With time, a map of one statistic for one time step. This needs a frame with polygons. Groups are drawn by colouring their areas. Without time, time series of chosen areas or groups, with the outer quantiles as a band. With data = TRUE, the observed prevalence (positives / tested) of every surveyed area and time step in the panel is added, with its exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% binomial interval. In a group's panel these are the surveyed areas of the group, while the band is for the group as a whole, so the two need not agree.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'stareal_pred'
plot(
  x,
  group = "area",
  time = NULL,
  ids = NULL,
  stat = "mean",
  data = TRUE,
  labels = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A stareal_pred.

group

"area" or one of the groupings predicted.

time

For a map: a time label (as in x$time$labels) or a time step number.

ids

For time series: the area or group ids to show (default: up to six, those with the most people tested first).

stat

For a map: the statistic to show (a column of the table, e.g. "mean", "q50", "p_gt_5").

data

For time series: add the observed prevalence and its exact binomial interval.

labels

For time series: panel titles in place of the ids. Either one per id, in the order of ids, or a vector named by id (ids not named keep their id). Labels must be unique.

...

Not used.

Value

A ggplot object (needs the ggplot2 package). Prevalence is in percent.

Examples

fr <- areal_lattice(4, 4)
sim <- simulate_areal(fr, time_frame(n_steps = 5), n_cells = 30, seed = 1)
fit <- fit_areal(sim, control = list(n_iter = 100, n_burn = 50, n_store = 25, n_chains = 1,
                                     ess_sweeps = 2, verbose = FALSE))
pr <- predict(fit, verbose = FALSE)
plot(pr, ids = c("r1c1", "r1c2"), labels = c("first unit", "second unit"))
